column1: # Author: Lane #1644 (Codex). Each compiled batch implementation read against its point/mode owner.

column8: The legacy auth method immediately calls its contextual method with Background. It does not use the embedded committed Engine batch; this is the same tx whose GetNode is overridden by storeTransaction. Public auth callback and generated Engine adapter passed aa83.

The auth contextual method calls s.tx.BatchGetNodesWithContext directly, retaining the same native pending/pinned data and ended lifecycle as s.tx.GetNode. Callback abort publication and pending-node outcomes passed aa83; the old committed adapter bypass was F-W3.

The graph-identity legacy entry delegates to its contextual method. That method owns request identity translation and returned-node provenance; this entry creates no second ordering or source selection.

The contextual graph-identity adapter resolves each original key with the retained identity lookup, deduplicates physical requests, dispatches the original Engine batch once and restores every original key while applying v.node. Its point method uses the same lookup and node projection. Generated adapter and public composite controls passed bab7/6fc5; it is not allowed to recover a bare physical adapter.

The public map-only compatibility entry delegates to BatchGetNodesContext over the issued FunctionStorage view; it retains its public signature and documented omission of failed IDs. Public BEGIN/new/change/delete controls and all7wrapper words passed both parsers in391b/e29f reds ->b459/a61b greens.

The error-returning public owner selects FunctionStorage once and performs elementwise point reads. It omits only not-found, joins other point failures, retains successful IDs and honors cancellation. Both-parser public BEGIN and real injected point-failure/partial-success controls passed b459/a61b.

The issued system graph batch is a literal empty map, matching systemGraphView.GetNode returning not-found for every supplied key. It must not delegate to the embedded administrative catalog. System issued-empty and generated adapter obligations passed both parser receipts.
The transaction wrapper legacy entry calls its contextual entry. No underlying committed batch call remains here; pending/pinned/ended semantics come from w.tx through that owner.

The contextual transaction adapter qualifies requested IDs through prefixNodeID, invokes the actual native tx batch, then restores requested keys and projects each returned node with toUserNode. Its point method qualifies and projects the same tx. Pending create/update/delete, retained snapshot and rollback refusal passed the public issued-batch schedule under all7wrapper words.

The search batch helper executes the optional light operation through ReadWithCapability. Its fallback uses the same issued point owner and omits only not-found. Its two actual public consumers are filtering and final hydration; the Search terminal correction now carries unrecovered errors, with current public green pending rather than a name-based exemption.

Continuation hydration selects a light batch through ReadWithCapability or the same issued full Engine batch, preserving errors. hydrateContinuationResultsContext immediately returns an error, validates authorization/missing members and applies existing result projection; full fallback payload is an explicit ordinary consumer, not D7 metadata.

Latest-visible batching retains its pendingReadConflict admission and invokes the exact GetNodeLatestVisible point operation per key. It now skips only errors.Is(ErrNotFound) and propagates every other failure. Qualified closed-native red7f32 lost ErrStorageClosed; current783 native properties passed within01a8, whose unrelated fixture assertions kept the whole job failed.

The Badger full legacy method delegates to its contextual entry. The shared native readNodeBatch owns the one captured read, buffered states, cache generation and body mode; this entry adds no capture.

The Badger contextual full entry selects readNodeBatch with embeddings=true. That flag selects full hydration/copying in the same existing withReadView capture used by point reads. Native generated full properties passed01a8.
The Badger embedding-free legacy entry delegates to its contextual entry. It does not synthesize a separate body read, snapshot or payload decoder.

The Badger contextual embedding-free entry selects readNodeBatch with embeddings=false, which uses body-only item hydration and copyNodeWithoutEmbeddings. Its actual point counterpart is GetNodeWithoutEmbeddings, rather than full GetNode. Generated mode properties passed01a8.

The native batch owner retains one withReadView capture, buffered/cache/physical precedence, decay policy and the selected body/embedding mode. It consumes the canonical copy functions. The D7 context correction extends that same copy owner; ordinary full/light point equivalence and native modes passed5261 and latest4469. It does not claim metadata-only payload cost.

The native transaction legacy method delegates to its contextual entry; unlike a committed Engine adapter it retains the transaction lifecycle check even for an empty request. Nonempty rollback refusal is part of the public transaction property schedule.

The native transaction contextual method locks the actual transaction once, checks ensureLifecycleActiveLocked and calls the extracted getNodeReadLocked visibleRead selector for each key. It preserves pending/deleted/pinned precedence and skips only not-found; there is no new read capture. Native transaction generated property and public Cypher/auth issued-view outcomes passed.

The public storage contextual entry immediately selects ordinary full batching through batchNodesWithContext(false). It retains the supplied Engine and delegates mode/admission decisions instead of unwrapping.

The full contextual branch now selects OwnedCapability on the original issued engine and otherwise calls that same core batch. The light branch keeps ReadWithCapability and exact contextual adaptation, preserving live support/refusal and errors; there is no physical unwrap.
The composite legacy method delegates to its contextual method. It contains no independent constituent ordering or first-source winner logic.

The composite contextual method provides child batch transport to c.resolveNodeReads and stores only emissions chosen by that same resolver used by GetNode. It does not choose a winner while iterating returned child maps. The resolver uses the catalog source selector and only required children. Public first/second collision red6e2f/91f2 became zero mismatches over256cases per wrapper in bab7/6fc5; required admission subjects also passed01a8.

The namespace full legacy entry delegates to its contextual owner. Both plain and accepted already-prefixed inputs retain their original map keys through the shared request-key join; generated key-domain red6b64 became green5261/7c89/bde2 and current4469.

The contextual namespace full entry retains the existing request PrefixNodeID owner, child batch and toUserNodeBatch. Original request IDs, including already-prefixed aliases, are now restored by the one materializer. Public generated key-domain cases passed current4469.

The namespace light legacy entry delegates to the same contextual namespace batch owner. Its admitted light-mode point counterpart is GetNodeWithoutEmbeddings, and its explicit unsupported-mode refusal remains authoritative. Accepted request-key cases passed current4469.

The contextual light namespace entry asks the same child operation and request-key join as the full path, while retaining truthful light-capability admission. Unsupported light batches explicitly refuse; admitted plain/prefixed key cases passed current4469.

Namespace readNodeBatch qualifies each request once with PrefixNodeID, then consumes the common batch dispatcher and passes original/physical arrays to toUserNodeBatch. The existing materializedReadWithContext owns cancellation and delivery; no second source selection exists.

toUserNodeBatch joins each original request with its already-qualified physical key through materializedKeyedWithContext, validates scope, uses canonical copy ownership and applies toUserNode. It never chooses a source or derives a response key from the returned node ID.

The remote legacy method binds the existing bounded defaultCtx and delegates to the contextual method. Its point GetNode uses the same remote entity query/decoder contract; this is transport lifetime, not a physical local capture.

The remote contextual method sends the same MATCH-by-ID entity query as point reads through readRemoteEntity and valueToNode for each supplied ID, omits returned ErrNotFound and propagates transport/decoder failures. No source-map merge or native fallback is introduced. Existing remote Engine public adapter property passed; remote lifetime/transport refusals remain carried by that adapter.
The tracing legacy method obtains its existing tracing context then delegates to the contextual method. It does not unwrap or replace the data view.

The tracing contextual method creates only an observation span and calls the common BatchGetNodesWithContext on its exact embedded Engine. No copy of identity selection or native batch preparation exists in tracing; wrapper grammar properties exercise both tracing/WAL orders.
The WAL legacy full batch delegates to its contextual method with Background. Reads create no WAL record and keep the exact data dependency.

The WAL contextual full batch calls the shared dispatcher with w.engine, preserving whatever issued namespace/transaction/view is carried there. It does not independently discover native storage or change result keys.
The WAL legacy light batch delegates to its contextual light method. It does not emulate vectors removal or claim capability by physically unwrapping.

The WAL contextual light batch calls the same common dispatcher with withoutEmbeddings=true. Its capability declaration/admission must retain the child light-mode availability, and the dispatcher enforces the exact contextual operation. This is forwarding through one generic cursor, not a second optional-capability walk.
